action: Focus scanning attention on the center of the image.
interpretation: Identify the 'hyperechoic horizontal line' located in the middle of the screen. Recognize this structure as the pleura.

action: Observe the pleural line for dynamic movement.
interpretation: Look for 'shimmering of the pleura.' Interpret this as evidence of motion of the pleural layers sliding against each other. Conclude that 'there is no pneumothorax' based on this finding.

action: Inspect the lateral edges of the image flanking the pleural line.
interpretation: Visualize 'ribbed shadows' on the sides of the pleura (acoustic shadowing from the ribs).

action: Prepare to change imaging modality to 'M mode' or 'motion mode'.
interpretation: Plan to use this modality to objectively confirm the motion of the pleura observed in 2D.

action: Activate M-mode cursor. 'Drop the line' directly in the middle of the screen.
interpretation: Ensure the sampling line crosses the pleura and lung tissue.

action: Hold the probe absolutely still to maintain the slice. Freeze the image to capture the M-mode tracing.
interpretation: Ensure stability to generate a clear graph without artifactual motion.

action: Analyze the near-field (top) of the frozen M-mode image.
interpretation: Observe that the top of the image consists of 'all horizontal lines.' Interpret this pattern as signifying 'no motion over time' in the superficial layers.

action: Correlate the horizontal line pattern with the anatomical layers.
interpretation: Identify this region as 'muscle and soft tissue.' Confirm this appearance is normal.
